WHAT is the Medical Reserve Corps?
The Medical Reserve Corps (MRC) is a national network of volunteers who help make their communities stronger and healthier during disasters and every day.

Volunteers are a part of a local community-based unit that works to improve emergency response capabilities, reduce potential public health risks and vulnerabilities, and build resiliency within a community.
MRC volunteers also regularly contribute to community preparedness —engaging in activities like health fairs and assisting with community vaccination clinics.
Austin/Travis County MRC is open to all volunteers over the age of 18.
Volunteers can include medical and public health professionals as well as any other community members without healthcare backgrounds who wish to donate their time and expertise.
